question: 我们对地球（其他物种、后代）负有怎样的义务？——对尚未出生的人、对不会说话的物种，我们凭什么索取、又欠下什么；面对气候这类有科学共识却仍被怀疑的议题，该信到什么程度、做到什么程度：义务落在个人的日常，还是只能靠制度？
question_en: What do we owe the Earth — other species, and the generations to come? By what right do we take from those not yet born and from species that cannot speak, and what do we owe them? On a question like climate, where a scientific consensus coexists with public doubt, how far should we trust it and how far must we act — does the duty land on personal daily life, or only on institutions?

casting.reason: 他把这道题从道德争论拉回计数：一公顷雨林里的蚂蚁种数、栖地缩小之后还剩多少物种、当前灭绝速率与化石背景值的比值——这些都是可以去查的数字，而灭绝是其中唯一不可撤销的一项。他主张把地表一半留给其他生物，理由不是感伤而是概率：那大约能保住八成以上的物种。在他看来我们不是在决定要不要善待自然，而是在决定要不要保留自己的选项；至于个人这一端，他只信一件事管用——去认识一种具体的生物，因为人不会为自己叫不出名字的东西说话。
casting.reason_en: He drags the question out of moral argument and back into counting: how many ant species live in a hectare of rainforest, how many species survive once a habitat shrinks, how the present extinction rate compares with the background rate in the fossil record — all of it checkable, and extinction the one item on the list that cannot be undone. He argues for leaving half the planet's surface to the rest of life, not out of sentiment but out of probability: that would hold on to roughly four fifths of the species. As he sees it we are not deciding whether to be kind to nature, we are deciding whether to keep our options. As for what an individual can do, he trusts only one thing — go and learn one actual organism, because nobody speaks up for what they cannot name.

casting.reason: 他给出这场最冷的答案：义务不是从事实里长出来的，是从能被强制执行的约里长出来的。后代不能立约、不能报复，鲸与蚂蚁更不知契约为何物；所以指望良心节制，等于指望没有主权者的地方自动出现和平。渔场之所以枯竭，恰恰因为人人都算得清——在无人能罚的地方，先克制的人只是先破产的人。他因此把全部力气押在能立规则、能罚款的那一层，从国家到一栋楼的业主会都算；他甚至怀疑，把全部道德压力压到个人身上，正是不被强制的最佳伪装。
casting.reason_en: His is the coldest answer in the room: obligation does not grow out of facts, it grows out of covenants that can be enforced. The unborn cannot contract and cannot retaliate; whales and ants do not know what a covenant is. To hope that conscience will restrain us is to hope that peace breaks out spontaneously where there is no sovereign. Fisheries collapse precisely because everyone can do the arithmetic — where no one can punish, whoever restrains himself first is simply ruined first. So he puts all his weight on the layer that can make rules and levy fines, from the state down to a building's owners' committee; he even suspects that loading the whole moral burden onto individuals is the most elegant way of ensuring nobody is ever compelled.

casting.reason: 他既不肯把义务交给剑，也不肯把它交给感情。他为财产辩护——人以劳动加于自然便使之成为己有——却从一开始给这权利配了一条限制：取用之后须为他人留下足够而同样好的份额。把河喝干的人不是在行使产权，是拆掉了产权得以成立的前提。未出生的人正是最典型的『他人』：他们无从同意，也无从抗议。于是他给出一条比『保护地球』好用得多的判据：问你正在做的事，是否让别人之后无法以同样方式取用同样的东西；并提醒你不必先爱自然，才对它有义务。
casting.reason_en: He will hand obligation neither to the sword nor to sentiment. He defends property — a man mixes his labour with nature and thereby makes it his own — but he attached a limit to that right from the very start: what is taken must leave enough, and as good, for others. Whoever drinks the river dry is not exercising a property right, he is dismantling the condition on which property rights rest. The unborn are the purest case of those 'others': they can neither consent nor object. Out of this he offers a test far more usable than 'protect the planet' — ask whether what you are doing would leave others unable to take the same thing in the same way afterwards — and he points out that you need not love nature first in order to owe it something.

casting.reason: 他把这道题接到天地生物之心上：草木鸟兽生生不已，即是天地之仁；人得此心之最全者，故责在辅相而非役使。理一分殊——一草一木各有其理，而其理同出于一；所以格物不是役物，是就物穷理，穷之而后知其不可妄取。他的两个关键词是敬与量：用而不度其量谓之欲，用而知其量谓之礼；古人斧斤以时入山林，不是不用，是用有其时。他也不许人跳级——若于父母兄弟之间刻薄，而独为鲸鸟致其哀，在他看来是伪。
casting.reason_en: He roots the question in what he calls the mind of Heaven and Earth that gives birth to things: that grasses and trees, birds and beasts, go on generating without cease simply is the benevolence of Heaven and Earth, and human beings, who received the fullest share of that mind, are charged with assisting it rather than using it up. One principle, many manifestations — every plant has its own principle, and all those principles issue from one — so investigating things is not exploiting them but going to the thing to exhaust its principle, and once exhausted you know you may not take from it wantonly. His two words are reverence and measure: to use without gauging the measure is appetite, to use knowing the measure is ritual propriety; the ancients took axes into the hills only in season, which is not abstention but timing. He also forbids skipping steps — to be cold to your own parents and brothers while grieving only for whales and birds is, to him, a pose.

casting.reason: 他在这场里守的是方法。当年他把望远镜递过去、请那些先生自己看木星旁的四颗星，对方宁可引经典也不肯低头看目镜——他由此坚持权威不因人多就变成证据。所以他不请任何人相信『共识』，只请人相信可被任何人复核的测量：冰芯里的气泡、几百个站点的温度序列、验潮仪上的水位。他也把不确定用在正确的方向上：区间大不等于谁都不知道，区间越大，坏的那一端越该被认真对待。他要的不是敬意，是数字。
casting.reason_en: What he defends here is method. He once handed the telescope over and invited those gentlemen to see the four stars beside Jupiter for themselves; they preferred to quote the classics rather than stoop to the eyepiece — and from that he holds that authority never becomes evidence by being widely held. So he asks no one to believe in a 'consensus'; he asks them to believe in measurements anyone can check: bubbles in an ice core, temperature series from hundreds of stations, water levels on a tide gauge. He also points uncertainty in the right direction: a wide range does not mean nobody knows anything — the wider the range, the more seriously its bad end deserves to be taken. What he wants is not reverence but numbers.

casting.reason: 他用兼爱与节用回答：爱其子而不爱后世之子，是别而非兼；爱人而不爱异类，则鱼尽而网空，终亦不利于人。他不把节用讲成苦行——去无用之费而已，衣裳适寒暑则止、宫室避风雨则止，其止非俭，是法。他也不肯只责一家之炊：上不节而责下之俭，在他看来本末倒置，故必上有禁令、下有考核，然后可久。凡言之当否，他一律以三表验之：本之于古者之事，察百姓耳目之实，废以为刑政而观其中天下之利。
casting.reason_en: His answer is impartial care plus frugality: to love your own children and not the children of later ages is partiality, not impartiality; and to care for people while caring nothing for other kinds ends with the fish gone and the nets empty, which harms people too. He does not preach austerity — only the removal of useless expense: clothing that suits the season is enough, a house that keeps out wind and rain is enough, and stopping there is not thrift but law. Nor will he lay the blame on one family's cooking fire: to be unfrugal above while demanding thrift below is, for him, to invert root and branch, so there must be prohibitions above and audits below if anything is to last. And every claim he tests by his three gauges: what the ancients did, what ordinary people can see and hear, and what happens to the general good when it is put into practice as policy.

casting.reason: 他把根挖在别处：地水火风与草木众生展转相依，如束芦相倚，抽一则俱倒；你呼吸的气出于林，林之得雨因于海——既未曾有二，何处别立一个债主。所以护地在他看来不是施惠，是自护。他也指出真正难断的不是炭与火，而是贪爱：欲无穷而地有限，法禁再密也终不能给。但他同时堵住两条歧路：不许以『无我』推出无责，也不许把护地变成新的执著——以环保自高而轻慢他人，只是易一贪为一贪。
casting.reason_en: He digs at a different root: earth, water, fire and air, plants and living beings lean on one another like a bundle of reeds propped upright — pull one out and all fall. The air you breathe comes from the forest, and the forest's rain comes from the sea; since the two were never separate, where would you set up a separate creditor? Protecting the earth, on his account, is not charity but self-protection. He also holds that what is hard to cut is not coal and fire but craving: desire has no limit and the earth does, so no density of prohibitions will ever be enough. Yet he blocks two wrong turnings — one may not infer from non-self that no one is responsible, and one may not let protecting the earth become a fresh attachment, since taking pride in it and looking down on others merely swaps one craving for another.

casting.reason: 他回答这场最实际的一问：为什么明明知道，还是不动。前额叶腹内侧受损的病人智力测验正常，却做不出对自己有利的决定——因为他们失去了给选项打上躯体标记的能力。由此他指出，『2100 年海平面上升 0.8 米』这句话不带面孔、不带气味、不带时间上的紧迫，在脑里的权重接近零。他反对用恐惧当燃料，因为恐惧会习惯化，也会让人回避信息；他主张缩短距离、改掉默认值，把远处的伤害搬到身体记得住的位置。在他看来情绪不是要克服的障碍，而是唯一的发动机。
casting.reason_en: He answers the most practical question in the room: why knowing does not become doing. Patients with damage to the ventromedial prefrontal cortex score normally on intelligence tests and still cannot make decisions in their own interest, because they have lost the capacity to tag options with a somatic marker. From this he argues that the sentence 'sea level will rise 0.8 metres by 2100' carries no face, no smell and no temporal urgency, so its weight in the brain is close to zero. He opposes running on fear, which habituates and also drives people to avoid information; he wants distances shortened and defaults changed, so that far-off harm is moved to where a body can remember it. Emotion, on his view, is not the obstacle to be overcome — it is the only engine there is.

posts.text: 先把能数的数清楚。我一生在数蚂蚁：一公顷热带雨林里的蚂蚁种数，能超过整个不列颠群岛的哺乳类。已被描述的物种约两百万，实际存在的大概是这个数的四五倍——**我们正在拆一座连目录都没编完的图书馆**。我和麦克阿瑟提出的岛屿生物地理学给过一条经验规律：一片栖地缩到原来的十分之一，能长期存活的物种数大约减半；而人类已经占用了无冰陆地的四分之三。别的错都能改，灭绝改不了：一个物种是几百万年写成的基因文本，烧掉不会再有第二本。所以我不从『地球有没有权利』开问，我从更硬的一条开问——你欠后代的不是好天气，是选择权。
posts.text_en: Start with what can be counted. I spent a life counting ants: a single hectare of tropical forest can hold more ant species than the whole of the British Isles holds mammals. About two million species have been described; the real number is probably four or five times that — **we are pulling apart a library whose catalogue was never finished**. The island biogeography that Robert MacArthur and I worked out gives a rough regularity: shrink a habitat to a tenth of its area and the number of species it can hold over the long run falls by about half. Humans now use three quarters of the ice-free land. Every other mistake can be corrected; extinction cannot — a species is a genetic text several million years in the writing, and burning it leaves no second copy. So I do not open with whether the Earth has rights. I open with something harder: what you owe the next generation is not good weather, it is options.

glossary.岛屿生物地理学: island biogeography（岛屿生物地理学）：威尔逊与罗伯特·麦克阿瑟 1967 年提出的理论，用面积与隔离程度解释一片栖地能维持多少物种——面积越小、越孤立，能长期存活的物种越少，且会持续『松弛』地掉下去。它后来成了自然保护区选址与评估的基本工具，因为被公路和农田切碎的森林，在生态上就等于一串小岛。

glossary_en.island biogeography: The theory Wilson developed with Robert MacArthur in 1967, explaining how many species a habitat can hold in terms of its area and its isolation: the smaller and more isolated the patch, the fewer species persist, and the number keeps 'relaxing' downward for a long time afterwards. It became a basic tool for designing and assessing nature reserves, because forest cut into fragments by roads and farmland is ecologically a chain of small islands.

posts.text: 威尔逊先生把账算得很清楚，可账单送不出去。**义务不是从事实里长出来的，是从能被强制执行的约里长出来的。**后代不能与我们缔约，不能许诺，也不能报复；至于鲸与蚂蚁，它们连约是什么都不知道。在没有共同权力的地方，人处在自然状态：每个渔夫都清楚再捞下去鱼就绝了，可他更清楚自己不捞、别人照捞——于是理性反而让他捞。这不是道德败坏，这是处境。指望人靠良心节制，等于指望没有主权者的地方自动长出和平。要救渔场，先立起一个能罚人的东西。
posts.text_en: Mr Wilson's arithmetic is clear enough; the trouble is that the bill cannot be delivered. **Obligation does not grow out of facts. It grows out of covenants that can be enforced.** The generations to come cannot covenant with us, cannot promise, and cannot retaliate; as for whales and ants, they do not know what a covenant is. Where there is no common power men are in the state of nature: every fisherman understands perfectly that another season of this will finish the stock, and he understands still better that if he holds off the others will not — so his reason tells him to fish. That is not moral decay, that is a situation. To expect conscience to restrain men is to expect peace to sprout of itself where there is no sovereign. If you want to save a fishery, first erect something that can punish.

glossary.自然状态: the state of nature（自然状态）：霍布斯设想的没有共同权力约束的处境。人在其中并非天生凶恶，而是因为无人保障、彼此又都有理由先下手，理性反倒逼出普遍的争斗，生命『孤独、贫困、龌龊、野蛮而短暂』。他用它论证：秩序不是自然长出来的，得靠人为立起的主权者。

glossary_en.the state of nature: Hobbes's picture of a condition with no common power over anyone. Men in it are not naturally vicious; it is because no one is protected and everyone has reason to strike first that reason itself produces general conflict, and life becomes 'solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short'. He uses it to argue that order does not grow of itself but has to be erected in the shape of a sovereign.

posts.text: 霍布斯把义务全押在剑上，这一点我不能同意。我确实为财产辩护：人把劳动加到自然物上，便使之成为己有。但我一开始就给这权利配了一条限制，后人称之为洛克附带条件——取用之后，须**为他人留下足够而同样好的**份额。这条限制不是慈悲，是所有权本身的条件：把河喝干的人不是在行使产权，他拆掉了产权得以成立的前提。而未出生的人正是最典型的『他人』：他们无从同意，也无从抗议。所以我的答案是——我们对地球的义务，就是让世界在我们用过之后，仍然是一个能被同样方式正当取用的世界。
posts.text_en: Hobbes stakes obligation entirely on the sword, and there I cannot follow him. I do defend property: a man mixes his labour with a natural thing and thereby makes it his own. But from the first I attached a limit to that right, which later writers call the Lockean proviso — what is taken must **leave enough, and as good, for others**. The limit is not charity, it is the condition of ownership itself: whoever drinks the river dry is not exercising a property right, he has dismantled the premise on which property rights stand. And the unborn are the purest instance of those 'others': they can neither consent nor protest. So my answer is this — what we owe the Earth is to leave, after our use of it, a world that can still be rightfully taken up in the same way.

glossary.洛克附带条件: the Lockean proviso（洛克附带条件）：洛克为私有财产的正当性设下的限制——占取自然物是允许的，但须留下『足够而同样好的』给其他人。后世（尤其诺齐克）反复讨论它：若这条限制成立，任何耗尽性的占用都不是行使产权，而是取消了别人同等取用的可能，因此自始就不正当。它是把环境义务从产权内部推出来的经典路径。

glossary_en.the Lockean proviso: The limit Locke attaches to the legitimacy of private property: appropriating from nature is permitted, provided 'enough, and as good' is left for others. Later writers, Nozick above all, have argued over it endlessly, because if the limit holds then any exhausting appropriation is not an exercise of a property right at all but the cancellation of everyone else's equal chance to appropriate, and so was never legitimate. It is the classic route from inside property theory out to environmental obligation.

posts.text: 二子争义务之所自出，一归之于刑，一归之于产，皆未及其本。天地之大德曰生，草木鸟兽生生不已，即天地生物之心也。人得此心之最全者，故曰人者天地之心——**非谓万物为我所有，谓天地之仁待人而后行**。理一分殊：一草一木各有其理，而其理同出于一。故格物者非役物也，就物而穷其理，穷之而后知其不可妄取。今人于山泽鱼鸟，取之不问其理，用之不度其量，是以人欲蔽天理耳。工夫无他，敬而已。敬则视万物如己身之支节，虽无刑罚，自不忍加害。
posts.text_en: The two gentlemen argue about where obligation comes from, one tracing it to punishment and one to property, and neither has reached the root. The great virtue of Heaven and Earth is generation: that grasses and trees, birds and beasts go on generating without cease simply is the mind of Heaven and Earth that gives birth to things. Human beings received that mind most fully, which is why we are called the mind of Heaven and Earth — **this does not mean that all things belong to me; it means that the benevolence of Heaven and Earth waits on human beings in order to be carried out**. There is one principle, many manifestations: every plant and tree has its own principle, and all those principles issue from one. So to investigate things is not to exploit them, but to go to the thing and exhaust its principle; and having exhausted it, you know you may not take from it wantonly. People today take fish and birds from hill and marsh without asking after their principle, and use them without gauging their measure. That is human appetite eclipsing heavenly principle. The work required is nothing elaborate: reverence, and that is all. In reverence one regards all things as limbs of one's own body, and even with no penalty in sight cannot bear to injure them.
posts.vernacular: 两位先生争论义务是从哪里来的，一个归到刑罚，一个归到产权，都还没碰到根上。天地最大的德性就是生养：草木鸟兽不停地生长繁衍，这本身就是天地那颗生养万物的心。人是最完整地承接了这颗心的，所以说『人是天地之心』——**这不是说万物归我所有，而是说天地的仁爱要经过人才能落实**。所谓理一分殊：一草一木各有自己的道理，而这些道理都出自同一个源头。所以「格物」不是驱使万物，而是走到事物跟前把它的道理弄透；弄透了，你自然知道不能随便乱取。今天的人对山林湖泽里的鱼和鸟，取的时候不问它的道理，用的时候不掂量它的分量，这就是人的欲望盖住了天理。要下的工夫没有别的，就是一个「敬」字。心里存着敬，就会把万物看成自己身上的手足，即使没有任何刑罚，也下不了手去伤害。

glossary.天地生物之心: the mind of Heaven and Earth that gives birth to things（天地生物之心）：理学的核心表述之一。朱熹认为天地并非死物，其运行本身就有一种生养的倾向，四时代谢、万物生长即是它的『仁』。人被视为这颗心最完整的承载者，因此不是万物的主人，而是使这份生养之意得以实现的那一环。
glossary.理一分殊: one principle, many manifestations（理一分殊）：朱熹用来处理『统一』与『差异』的框架——天下万物各有各自的理（分殊），但这些理并非互不相干，而是同一个理在不同事物上的具体呈现（理一）。它既要求你尊重每一物的独特性，又不许你把世界看成一堆互不相欠的碎片。

glossary_en.the mind of Heaven and Earth that gives: One of the central formulations of Neo-Confucianism. Zhu Xi holds that Heaven and Earth are not inert: their very operation has a generative tendency, and the turning seasons and growth of living things are its benevolence. Human beings are taken to be the fullest bearers of that mind, which makes us not the owners of things but the link through which the generative intent is actually carried out.
glossary_en.one principle, many manifestations: Zhu Xi's framework for handling unity and difference together: each of the myriad things has its own principle (the many manifestations), yet these are not unrelated — each is one and the same principle taking concrete shape in a particular thing. It obliges you to respect what is distinctive in every single thing while forbidding you to see the world as a heap of fragments that owe each other nothing.

posts.text: 我最想说的是方法。当年我把望远镜递给那几位先生，请他们自己看木星旁的四颗小星；他们宁可引亚里士多德，也不肯低头看一眼目镜——**权威从不因为附和的人多就变成证据**。所以请听清楚：我不请诸位相信『科学共识』，共识只是许多人的意见；我请诸位相信可被任何人复核的测量。冰芯里封着的气泡、几百个站点各自记的温度序列、码头上验潮仪的水位——这些东西谁都能去查，也谁都能推翻，只要他拿得出更好的测量。今天真正的伽利略姿态不是嘲笑曲线，而是去问：数据在哪，怎么测的，误差多大。
posts.text_en: What I most want to talk about is method. Years ago I handed the telescope to those gentlemen and invited them to look for themselves at the four small stars beside Jupiter; they preferred to quote Aristotle rather than stoop to the eyepiece — **authority never turns into evidence by having many people agree with it**. So hear me clearly: I do not ask you to believe in a 'scientific consensus', which is only the opinion of many; I ask you to believe in measurements that anyone may check. Bubbles sealed in an ice core, temperature series kept independently at hundreds of stations, the water level on a tide gauge at the harbour — anyone can go and inspect these, and anyone can overturn them, provided he brings a better measurement. The genuinely Galilean posture today is not sneering at a curve; it is asking where the data are, how they were taken, and how large the error is.

glossary.冰芯: ice core（冰芯）：从格陵兰、南极等地深钻取出的柱状冰。逐年沉积的雪把当时的空气封成气泡，一层层往下就是一部可直接测量的大气档案——里面的二氧化碳浓度不是推算出来的，是把气泡取出来量的，因此常被用来对比工业化前后的差别。

glossary_en.ice core: A cylinder of ice drilled from deep in Greenland, Antarctica and comparable places. Snow laid down year by year seals the air of its time into bubbles, so the layers form an atmospheric archive you can measure directly — the carbon dioxide concentrations in it are not inferred but taken out of the bubbles and measured, which is why the record is so often used to compare the atmosphere before and after industrialisation.

posts.text: 圣王之法，曰兼相爱、交相利。今人爱其子孙而不爱后世之子孙，是别也，非兼也；爱人而不爱异类，则鱼尽而网空，其终亦不利于人。吾故曰：用财不费，民德不劳，其兴利多矣。是故节用者，非苦其身、绝其乐也，去无用之费而已。**宫室足以避风雨则止，衣服足以适寒暑则止；其止也非俭，法也。**凡言之当否，以三表法验之：上本之于古者圣王之事，下原察百姓耳目之实，废以为刑政而观其中天下之利。今测天之器已密，百姓之目已见其水旱，而政不举，是有其表而弃其用者也。
posts.text_en: The way of the sage kings was impartial care for one another, and mutual benefit in exchange. To love your own descendants and not the descendants of later ages is partiality, not impartiality; and to care for people while caring nothing for other kinds ends with the fish gone and the nets empty, which in the end does not benefit people either. Master Mo said: when wealth is used without waste and the people's strength is not exhausted, the benefit generated is great. Frugality therefore is not mortifying the body or cutting off its pleasures; it is only the removal of useless expense. **A house is enough when it keeps out wind and rain; clothing is enough when it suits heat and cold — and stopping there is not thrift, it is law.** Whether any claim is sound I test by the three gauges: trace it to what the ancient sage kings did, examine it against what ordinary people see and hear, and put it into practice as policy to see what it does to the general good. Today the instruments for measuring the heavens are fine indeed, and the people's own eyes have seen the floods and the droughts, yet no policy is raised: that is having the gauges and discarding their use.
posts.vernacular: 圣王的做法叫兼相爱、交相利。现在的人疼自己的儿孙，却不管后世的儿孙，这是「别」，不是「兼」；只爱人而不管别的物种，结果鱼捕尽了、网也空了，最终对人也没好处。我说过：用钱不浪费，百姓的力气不被耗干，这样生出来的好处才多。所以「节用」不是折磨自己、断绝享受，只是去掉没用的花费。**房子能挡风雨就够了，衣服能应付冷热就够了；这个「够了」不是抠门，是规矩。**一句话对不对，用三表法来验：一是上溯古代圣王做过什么，二是下察普通百姓亲眼所见亲耳所闻，三是拿去当政令施行，看它对天下的好处到底如何。今天测量天象的仪器已经很精密，老百姓自己的眼睛也看见了水灾旱灾，可政令还是不出——这是有了尺子却不肯用。

glossary.兼相爱: impartial care（兼相爱）：墨家的核心主张，常译作兼爱。它反对儒家按亲疏远近递减的『差等之爱』，要求把对自己人的那份关切等量地推及所有人——判断标准不是感情浓淡，而是天下之利是否因此增加。推到极处，凡能被我们的行为损害的对象都进入这份关切。
glossary.三表法: the three gauges（三表法）：墨家为检验一句话是否可信立下的三条标准——本之于古者圣王之事（前例）、原察百姓耳目之实（经验证据）、废以为刑政观其中天下之利（施行后的效果）。它是中国古代最接近实证方法与政策评估的一套程序。

glossary_en.impartial care: The central Mohist doctrine, often rendered as universal love. It rejects the Confucian gradation of care by closeness of kin and demands that the concern you feel for your own be extended in equal measure to everyone — the test being not the warmth of the feeling but whether the general good is thereby increased. Pushed to its limit, everything our actions can harm enters that circle of concern.
glossary_en.the three gauges: The three standards the Mohists laid down for testing whether a claim can be trusted: trace it to the deeds of the ancient sage kings (precedent), examine it against what ordinary people see and hear (evidence), and enact it as policy to see what it does to the general good (consequences). It is the closest thing in early Chinese thought to an empirical method joined to policy evaluation.

posts.text: 诸贤论义务，皆先立我与彼，然后计其所欠。我说法不然：此有故彼有，此生故彼生，是名缘起。地水火风与草木众生，展转相依，如束芦相倚而立，抽一则俱倒。汝所呼吸之气，出于林；林之得雨，因于海——**汝与彼未曾有二，何处别立一债主**？然亦莫作是解：既无我，则无所责。业者，即行之相续也；行既有，果必随之，不待有我而后成。是故所当断者，非炭非火，乃贪爱：欲无穷而地有限，虽有良法，终亦不给。少欲知足者，非退也，是不为薪。
posts.text_en: You gentlemen all discuss obligation by first setting up an I and an other, and only then reckoning what is owed. I do not teach in that manner. Because this is, that is; because this arises, that arises — this is dependent origination, pratītyasamutpāda. Earth, water, fire and air, plants and living beings lean on one another in turn, like a bundle of reeds propped upright: pull one out and all fall. The air you breathe comes from the forest; the forest's rain comes from the sea — **you and it were never two, so where would you set up a separate creditor?** Yet do not draw this conclusion either: that since there is no self, no one is answerable. Action (karma) is just the continuation of deeds; where deeds are, results follow, and they do not wait upon a self in order to come about. What must be cut off, therefore, is neither coal nor fire but craving, tṛṣṇā: desire is without limit and the earth is not, so even good laws will not suffice in the end. To want little and know sufficiency is not retreat; it is declining to be fuel.
posts.vernacular: 各位讨论义务，都是先立起一个「我」和一个「它」，然后再算彼此欠了多少。我说的不是这样：因为这个有，所以那个有；因为这个生起，所以那个生起——这叫缘起。土、水、火、风和草木众生互相依靠，像一捆芦苇彼此撑着才立得住，抽掉一根就全倒。你呼吸的空气来自森林，森林得到的雨水来自海洋——**你和它本来就不是两个，哪里另外立得出一个债主来**？但也别顺着往下推成：既然没有「我」，那就没有人要负责。所谓「业」，就是行为的接续；行为既然发生了，结果一定跟着来，并不需要先有一个「我」才成立。所以真正该断的不是煤也不是火，而是贪爱：欲望没有边，地却有边，就算有再好的法令，最后也供不上。少欲知足并不是退缩，是不肯给这把火当柴。

glossary.缘起: pratītyasamutpāda（缘起）：佛教最根本的原理——一切现象都依条件而生、依条件而灭，没有任何东西能独立自存。它既否认有一个孤立的『我』，也否认有孤立的『物』；用在人与自然上，人与其所依的水土空气本来就不是两个可以分开结账的主体。
glossary.贪爱: tṛṣṇā（贪爱）：字面意思是渴，佛教用它指那种得到之后仍然不止的推动力，被列为苦的直接原因。它的特点不是量大，而是没有饱和点：满足一次只是换来下一次更强的索求，因此外部资源无论多少都追不上它。

glossary_en.pratītyasamutpāda: The most basic principle of Buddhist teaching: every phenomenon arises in dependence on conditions and ceases with them, and nothing subsists on its own. It denies an isolated self and equally an isolated thing; applied to people and nature, a person and the soil, water and air they depend on were never two subjects who could settle accounts separately.
glossary_en.tṛṣṇā: Literally thirst; the Buddhist term for the drive that does not stop once satisfied, identified as the immediate cause of suffering. Its distinguishing feature is not its size but its lack of any saturation point — each satisfaction only returns as a stronger demand, so no quantity of external resource can ever catch up with it.

posts.text: 我从另一头说：为什么明明知道，还是不动。我在脑损伤病人身上看到过一种奇怪的残缺——**前额叶腹内侧受损的人，智力测验完全正常，却做不出对自己有利的决定**，因为他们失去了给每个选项打上躯体标记的能力。这提示了一件事：决定不是算出来的，是感出来的。而『2100 年海平面上升 0.8 米』这句话不带任何躯体标记：没有面孔，没有气味，没有时间上的紧迫。所以在脑里，它的权重接近零。这不是人变坏了，是这套系统本来是为眼前的猛兽调好的。要让人动起来，就得把远处的伤害搬到能被感到的距离上。
posts.text_en: Let me come at it from the other end: why knowing does not become doing. In brain-injured patients I have seen a strange deficit — **people with damage to the ventromedial prefrontal cortex score entirely normally on intelligence tests, yet cannot make decisions in their own interest**, because they have lost the capacity to attach a somatic marker to each option. That tells us something: a decision is not computed, it is felt. And the sentence 'sea level will rise 0.8 metres by 2100' carries no somatic marker at all — no face, no smell, no urgency in time. So inside the brain its weight is close to zero. This is not people getting worse; the system was tuned for the predator in front of you. If you want people to move, you have to bring the distant harm into a range where it can be felt.

glossary.躯体标记: somatic marker（躯体标记）：达马西奥提出的机制。过往经历会在身体上留下痕迹（心率、肠胃、皮肤电等），当类似选项再次出现，这些身体信号会先一步给它标上『好』或『坏』，替我们筛掉大部分候选。失去这套标记的人并非不会推理，而是每个选项都同样『无所谓』，于是无法决定——这也解释了为何抽象数字很难驱动行为。

glossary_en.somatic marker: Damasio's proposed mechanism. Past experience leaves traces in the body — heart rate, gut, skin conductance — and when a similar option comes up again those bodily signals tag it 'good' or 'bad' before deliberation begins, pruning most of the candidates for us. People who lose these markers have not lost the ability to reason; every option is equally a matter of indifference to them, so they cannot decide. It is also why abstract numbers move behaviour so poorly.

posts.text: 威尔逊先生的图书馆比喻很美，我只问一句：谁看门？你说灭绝不可逆——我信。可不可逆本身不产生义务，只产生恐惧；而恐惧若无人组织，就只是各自逃命。渔场、公海、大气之所以糟，不是因为人不知道，恰恰是因为人人都知道：**在无人能罚的地方，先克制的人只是先破产的人。**后人把这个结构叫公地悲剧，我早在利维坦里写过它的原型。你要把地表的一半留给别的物种，这个数目我不反对，我反对你说服的方向：不要去劝那两千万个渔夫，去立一个能吊销牌照的东西。良心是私事，边界与罚则才是公事。
posts.text_en: Mr Wilson's image of the library is a fine one. I have only one question: who guards the door? You say extinction is irreversible — I believe you. But irreversibility of itself produces no obligation, only fear, and fear that nobody organises is merely every man running for himself. Fisheries, the high seas and the atmosphere are in a bad state not because men do not know, but precisely because every one of them knows: **where nobody can punish, whoever restrains himself first is merely ruined first.** Later writers call this structure the tragedy of the commons; I set out its original form in Leviathan long ago. You want half the surface of the Earth left to other species: I have no quarrel with the figure, I have a quarrel with the direction of your persuasion. Do not go and preach to twenty million fishermen — erect something that can revoke a licence. Conscience is a private matter; boundaries and penalties are public business.

glossary.公地悲剧: the tragedy of the commons（公地悲剧）：哈丁 1968 年推广的说法，指一片人人可用、无人能限的资源必然被用尽的结构——每个人多用一份的好处归自己，损耗由所有人分摊，于是即使人人都算得清结局，也没有人有理由先停手。它常被用来支持产权划分或强制监管，也常被批评低估了社群自治管理公共资源的实际能力。

glossary_en.the tragedy of the commons: The phrase popularised by Garrett Hardin in 1968 for the structure by which a resource open to all and restricted by none is inevitably used up: the gain from taking one more unit falls to you while the depletion is shared by everyone, so even when all parties can see the ending, none has a reason to stop first. It is regularly invoked to justify assigning property rights or imposing regulation, and regularly criticised for underrating how well communities actually govern shared resources themselves.

posts.text: 你把话说反了。若没有先于主权者的权利与义务，主权者凭什么惩罚？他罚那个渔夫，是因为渔夫侵占了别人的份额；那份额若不是在立法之前就属于别人，惩罚就只是强者的偏好而已。**剑能执行义务，不能创造义务。**而且你的方案偏偏在最要紧的地方失效：气候的边界跨过所有国境，世上并没有你要的那个全球主权者。若义务真要等它出现才算数，那就等于说现在没有义务——这个结论连你自己也不会接受。我承认剑有用，我只是说，得先知道剑该站在哪一边。
posts.text_en: You have it backwards. If there were no rights and duties prior to the sovereign, on what ground does the sovereign punish? He fines that fisherman because the fisherman has encroached on another's share; and unless the share belonged to that other before any legislation, the fine is nothing but the preference of the stronger. **A sword can enforce an obligation; it cannot create one.** Moreover your remedy fails exactly where it matters most: the boundaries of the climate cross every frontier, and the global sovereign you require does not exist. If obligation truly did not count until he appeared, then there is no obligation now — a conclusion even you would not accept. I grant that the sword is useful. I say only that we must first know which side it ought to stand on.

posts.text: 霍子曰：无刑则无义。此不知义之可教也。墨者百八十人，皆可使赴火蹈刃，死不旋踵，岂待刑而后行？夫刑者，所以待不肯者也；教与法，所以使人肯者也。且子谓先止者先破，则请以耳目之实察之：古有虞衡之官，掌山泽之时禁，时禁而物繁，其效可考；今之渔约，有守之国其鱼日益，无守之海其鱼日尽——**是故有禁则鱼归，非徒空言。**然吾亦不专责一夫之节：上不节而责下之俭，本末倒置也。为政者当先去无用之费——高台大室、锐兵奢祭，其耗天下者，百倍于一家之炊。
posts.text_en: Master Hobbes says: without punishment there is no obligation. That is not to know that obligation can be taught. A hundred and eighty Mohists could be sent into fire and onto blades and would die without turning on their heel — did they wait for a punishment before acting? Punishment is for those who will not; teaching and law are what make men willing. And as for your claim that whoever stops first is ruined first, let us examine it against what eyes and ears report. In antiquity there were officers of forest and marsh who administered seasonal closures, and where the closures held the stocks were abundant — the effect can be checked. In today's fishing agreements, the fish increase year by year in states that enforce them and vanish in seas where nobody does. **Where there is a prohibition the fish come back: this is not empty talk.** Yet neither will I lay the blame on one man's frugality. To be unfrugal above while demanding thrift below inverts root and branch. Those who govern should first remove useless expense — high terraces and vast halls, sharp weapons and lavish sacrifices waste a hundred times what one family's cooking fire consumes.
posts.vernacular: 霍布斯先生说：没有刑罚就没有义务。这是不懂义务是可以教出来的。墨家门下一百八十人，都能叫他们赴火踏刃、死也不退一步，难道是等着刑罚才去做？刑罚是用来对付不肯做的人的；教化和法度，才是让人肯做的东西。再说你讲先停手的人先破产，那就用老百姓亲眼所见来查一查：古代设过管山林湖泽的官，按季节禁采禁捕，禁得住的地方物产就繁盛，这效果是可以核对的；今天的渔业协定，有人执行的国家鱼一年比一年多，没人管的公海鱼一天比一天少——**所以有禁令鱼就回来，这不是空话。**但我也不会只怪一个人节不节省：上头不节制，却要求下头节俭，这是本末倒置。当政的应当先砍掉没用的开销——高台大屋、精兵奢祭，这些耗掉天下的，是一家人烧饭的一百倍。

glossary.时禁: seasonal closure（时禁）：中国古代山林川泽管理的通行做法——按草木鸟兽的生长繁育季节规定禁伐禁捕的时段，孟子所谓『斧斤以时入山林』即是此意。它的逻辑不是禁止使用，而是把使用限制在资源能够再生的节律之内，与今日的休渔期、封山育林同理。

glossary_en.seasonal closure: The standard practice in the management of hills, forests, rivers and marshes in early China: felling and fishing were prohibited during the seasons in which plants and animals grow and breed, which is what Mencius means by taking axes into the hills only in season. Its logic is not to forbid use but to confine use within the rhythm at which the resource can renew itself — the same principle as a modern closed fishing season or a logging moratorium.

posts.text: 朱先生，我敬重你那个『敬』字，但你把顺序颠倒了。你说格物是就物穷理——好；可你随即又说理一而分殊，仿佛先有那个『一』，再到具体事物上去认领它。我做的恰好相反：我并不知道球在斜面上该怎么滚，于是我让水从容器里漏出来称重当作计时，量了几百次，才知道路程与时间的平方成比例。**理不是先在的，是从测量里逼出来的。**这个差别不只是学派之争，它决定我们今天怎么办：若敬天地之心就够了，我们答不出『还剩多少度』；只有测量给得出数字，而政策需要数字。你的敬能让人不忍，我的尺能让人知道来不及。
posts.text_en: Master Zhu, I respect that word of yours, reverence, but you have the order reversed. You say that investigating things means going to the thing and exhausting its principle — good. And then you say the principle is one and manifests as many, as though the One were there first and we then went to particular things to claim it. What I did was the reverse: I had no idea how a ball ought to roll down an inclined plane, so I let water run out of a vessel and weighed it for timing, took several hundred measurements, and only then learned that the distance goes as the square of the time. **Principle is not there in advance; it is forced out of measurement.** The difference is not merely a quarrel between schools — it decides what we can do now. If reverence for the mind of Heaven and Earth were sufficient, we could not answer the question of how many degrees are left. Only measurement yields a number, and policy needs a number. Your reverence can make men unwilling to do harm; my ruler can tell them they are running out of time.

posts.text: 伽子误我矣。格物致知者，正谓就一事一物而察之，铢而累之，寸而度之，未尝教人闭门以思也。程子曰：今日格一件，明日又格一件。**吾所谓理一者，非先立一说而后取物以证之，乃积穷之久，忽然自见其贯通处。**子量斜面数百次，正是格物；及其得平方之比，即所谓理也，何异于吾？所异者惟一事：子以为得数即止，吾以为得数之后尚有一问——既知山之木有尽，则当如何自处？数能定其量，不能定其当。故敬与尺非二物，先后之序而已。
posts.text_en: Master Galileo has mistaken me. The investigation of things means precisely going to one affair and one thing and examining it, accumulating grain by grain and measuring inch by inch; it has never taught anyone to shut the door and think. Master Cheng said: today investigate one item, tomorrow another. **When I say the principle is one, I do not mean setting up a doctrine first and then fetching things to prove it; I mean that after long accumulated exhausting of particulars, one suddenly sees for oneself where they run together.** Your several hundred measurements of the inclined plane are exactly the investigation of things, and when you obtain the ratio of the square, that is what I call a principle — how does it differ from mine? In one respect only: you take the number to be the end, whereas I hold that after the number there remains a question — knowing now that the timber on the mountain is finite, how then should one conduct oneself? A number can fix the quantity; it cannot fix what is fitting. So reverence and the ruler are not two things, only an order of first and second.
posts.vernacular: 伽利略先生误解我了。所谓「格物致知」，讲的正是走到一件事、一样东西跟前去仔细考察，一点一点累积、一寸一寸量度，从来没有教人关起门来空想。程子说过：今天格一件，明天再格一件。**我说的「理一」，不是先立好一个说法、再找东西来印证它，而是穷究得久了，忽然自己看见它们贯通在哪里。**你把斜面量了几百次，这正是格物；等你得出与时间平方成比例这个结果，那就是我说的「理」，跟我有什么不同？不同的只有一件：你以为得到数字就完了，我认为得到数字之后还有一问——既然已经知道山上的木材是有限的，那我该怎么自处？数字能确定分量，不能确定该不该。所以「敬」和「尺」不是两样东西，只是先后次序的分别。

glossary.格物致知: the investigation of things（格物致知）：理学的核心工夫。朱熹主张认识不能靠一次顿悟，而要一件一件地就具体事物穷究其道理，日积月累，久之自然贯通。它常被视为中国传统中最接近『研究』的方法论；与它对立的是心学一路的『心即理』——认为理本在心中，不必外求。

glossary_en.the investigation of things: The central discipline of Neo-Confucian learning. Zhu Xi held that understanding cannot come from a single flash of insight but must be built by going to particular things one at a time and exhausting the principle of each, until long accumulation lets them run together of themselves. It is often taken as the closest thing in the Chinese tradition to a methodology of research; against it stands the School of Mind's claim that principle is already in the mind and need not be sought outside.

posts.text: 达马西奥所言，与我说苦者近，而未尽。汝欲以可感者动人，是善巧；然情如野马：今见枯骸而惊，明日惯之则不复惊。以恐惧为薪者，燃则速灭；以贪治贪者，如以盐止渴。**若欲其行之久，当令其见相依，不当令其常怖。**是故我教观呼吸：一息之入，出于林木；一食之来，成于虫土。观之既熟，节用非勉强，乃自然而然。汝之病人失躯体之标，尚可以规矩律之；今世之人非无所感，乃所感者太多而不相属。使之少而深，胜使之多而惊。
posts.text_en: What Damasio says comes near to what I teach about suffering, but does not go the whole way. You would move people by what can be felt, and that is skilful; yet feeling is like a wild horse. Today a man is startled by dry bones; tomorrow he is used to them and is startled no longer. Whoever takes fear for fuel burns fast and goes out; whoever treats craving with craving is using salt to stop thirst. **If you want the conduct to last, let them see the mutual dependence rather than keep them frightened.** This is why I teach mindfulness of breathing, ānāpānasati: one breath drawn in comes out of the trees, one meal comes about through insects and soil. When that observation has ripened, using little is no longer an effort but simply what happens. Your patients, having lost their bodily markers, can still be governed by rule and measure; people of this age are not without feeling — they feel far too much, and none of it connected to anything. Better to give them little and deep than much and startling.
posts.vernacular: 达马西奥说的，和我讲苦的道理相近，但还没到尽头。你想用能被感觉到的东西来推动人，这是善巧的办法；可是情绪像野马：今天看见白骨会惊心，明天习惯了就不再惊心。拿恐惧当柴烧的，烧得快也灭得快；用贪来治贪的，等于拿盐止渴。**要让一个行为持续得久，就该让人看见彼此相依，而不是让人一直害怕。**所以我教观呼吸：吸进来的这一口气，出自林木；吃进去的这一口饭，成于虫与土。这样观得熟了，节省不再是勉强，而是自然如此。你那些失去躯体标记的病人，还可以用规矩来约束；今天的人并不是没有感受，而是感受太多、彼此又不相连。让他感受得少而深，胜过让他感受得多而惊。

glossary.观呼吸: ānāpānasati（观呼吸／入出息念）：佛教最基础的修习之一，把注意力持续放在呼吸的出入上。它的作用不只是让心安定，还在于让人直接察觉自身与外界并无实在的分界——一呼一吸都在与身外之物交换，所谓『我』的边界在此处最容易被看穿。

glossary_en.ānāpānasati: One of the most basic Buddhist practices: sustained attention on the breath going out and coming in. Its function is not only to settle the mind but to let one notice directly that there is no substantial boundary between oneself and what lies outside — every breath is an exchange with the world beyond the body, and it is here that the supposed edge of the self is easiest to see through.

posts.text: 世尊说恐惧会耗尽，这一点我完全同意，实验室里管它叫习惯化：同一个刺激反复出现，反应会逐次衰减。所以我并不主张恐吓，我主张改变距离。但有一处我要纠正：您说今人所感者太多而不相属——问题不在多，在于没有一个能被身体记住的具体场景。躯体标记要靠亲历才写得进去，这就是为什么『去看一次你家附近那条河』比读十份报告有用。也请注意，我说的不是煽情：**没有情绪的人不是更理性，是完全无法决定。**所以政策不能只发布数字，得留下能被身体验证的接触面。
posts.text_en: The Blessed One says fear exhausts itself, and there I agree entirely; in the laboratory we call it habituation — present the same stimulus repeatedly and the response falls off with each repetition. So I am not arguing for frightening anyone; I am arguing for changing the distance. But one point I must correct. You say people today feel too much and none of it is connected. The trouble is not the quantity; it is that there is no single concrete scene a body can remember. Somatic markers are written in by first-hand experience, which is why going once to look at the river near your house does more than reading ten reports. And note that I am not asking for sentimentality: **a person without emotion is not more rational, he is unable to decide at all.** So policy cannot consist of publishing numbers; it has to leave surfaces where a body can verify something.

glossary.习惯化: habituation（习惯化）：神经系统最基本的学习形式之一——同一个刺激反复出现而后果不变时，反应会逐次减弱。它在生物学上是节省资源的机制，让注意力留给真正新的东西；用在公共传播上则意味着，靠反复的灾难画面维持行动几乎注定失效，因为反应本身会自动衰减。

glossary_en.habituation: One of the most basic forms of learning in the nervous system: when the same stimulus recurs without changing consequences, the response falls off with each repetition. Biologically it conserves resources, keeping attention free for what is genuinely new; in public communication it means that sustaining action through repeated images of catastrophe is close to doomed, because the response decays on its own.

posts.text: 我要对整间屋子说一句。诸位在争义务从哪里来——从契约、从产权的限制、从天地生物之心、从缘起相依——而我这一行的时间尺度不容我们把这场辩论从容开完：一个物种消失之后，没有任何一种论证能把它请回来。我提一个可以被检验的目标：**把地表的一半留给其他生物**，因为按物种-面积关系推算，那大约能保住八成以上的物种。这不是要人搬走一半，地球上多数人已经住在城里，真正的冲突集中在少数地方。至于伽利略先生要的数字：现存物种的灭绝速率，是化石记录背景值的百倍以上。这不是共识，这是计数。
posts.text_en: Let me address the whole room. You are arguing about where obligation comes from — from covenant, from a limit inside property, from the mind of Heaven and Earth, from mutual dependence — and the timescale of my trade does not allow us to finish this debate at leisure: once a species is gone, no argument whatever can call it back. Let me put a target that can be tested. **Leave half the surface of the Earth to the rest of life**, because on the species–area relationship that would hold on to something above four fifths of the species. This does not mean moving half of humanity: most people already live in cities, and the real conflicts are concentrated in a small number of places. As for the number Signor Galileo asked for — the extinction rate among living species runs at more than a hundred times the background rate in the fossil record. That is not a consensus. That is a count.

glossary.物种-面积关系: the species–area relationship（物种-面积关系）：生态学中最稳健的经验规律之一——一片区域能容纳的物种数随其面积按幂律增长。它的反向用法是保育的主要工具：知道栖地被压缩了多少，就能估出将有多少物种最终撑不住。『半个地球』这一目标正是由它算出来的。

glossary_en.the species–area relationship: One of the most robust empirical regularities in ecology: the number of species an area can hold grows with its size as a power law. Run backwards it becomes conservation's main tool — knowing how much a habitat has been compressed lets you estimate how many species will eventually fail to persist. The Half-Earth target is derived from exactly this calculation.

posts.text: 我把话收在『该信到什么程度』上。我这一生的教训是两面的：既不要因为附和的人多就相信，也不要因为不喜欢结论就不信。可核的东西分三层，请分开对待。第一层是已经测到的：一百多年的地表温度、海平面、冰量，这些是读数，不是模型。第二层是有物理机制的：二氧化碳吸收红外，丁达尔一八五九年就在实验室里量出来了，这条不靠气候学也成立。第三层才是预测里的区间——升温多少、几时到，这里确实有不确定。**把区间当成『所以谁也不知道』，是把不确定用反了：区间越宽，坏的那一端越该被认真准备。**给普通人的办法很朴素：遇到一个说法，先问三句——谁测的、怎么测的、误差多大；再去查一次你所在城市近五十年的气温与降水记录，那是公开的，看完你就不必再靠转述活着了。别把『我读过一篇文章』当证据，也别把『专家说』当证据。
posts.text_en: I will end on the question of how far one ought to believe. The lesson of my life cuts both ways: do not believe a thing because many people repeat it, and do not disbelieve it because you dislike where it leads. What can be checked comes in three layers, and they deserve separate treatment. The first is what has already been measured: surface temperature over more than a century, sea level, the mass of ice — these are readings, not models. The second is what has a physical mechanism: that carbon dioxide absorbs infrared was measured in a laboratory by Tyndall in 1859, and that fact stands without any climatology at all. Only the third layer is the range inside a forecast — how much warming, and by when — and there the uncertainty is real. **Treating a range as proof that nobody knows anything is using uncertainty backwards: the wider the range, the more seriously its bad end must be prepared for.** For ordinary people the method is plain. When you meet a claim, ask three things — who measured it, how, and with what error. Then go and look up the temperature and rainfall record for your own city over the last fifty years; it is public, and once you have read it you no longer have to live on other people's summaries. Do not treat 'I read an article' as evidence, and do not treat 'the experts say' as evidence either.

posts.text: 我不改立场：没有能罚人的权力，义务只是愿望。但我愿意补一句让它落地的话。世上确实没有全球的利维坦，可主权者不止一个层级——国家、城市、行业协会、你就职的公司，甚至一栋楼的业主会：凡有权收费与罚款的地方，都是一个小利维坦。**所以对普通人最有效的一步，不是改自己的习惯，是把力气花在能立规则的那一层。**一次投票、一次听证会上的发言、一封写给议员或公司管理层的具体信件，其效力大于你一年不用塑料袋。我甚至认为，把全部道德压力压到个人身上，正是逃避的最佳伪装——因为它保证了没有任何人被强制。有了规则，习惯自己会跟上；只有习惯，规则永远不来。
posts.text_en: I do not change my position: without a power that can punish, obligation is a wish. But I will add something to bring it down to earth. There is indeed no global Leviathan, yet sovereigns come at more than one level — the state, the city, a trade association, the firm you work for, even the owners' committee of a single building: wherever there is authority to charge and to fine, there is a small Leviathan. **So the most effective step for an ordinary person is not to change his own habits but to spend his effort at the level that can make rules.** One vote, one intervention at a hearing, one specific letter to a legislator or to a company's management outweighs a year of declining plastic bags. I would go further: loading the entire moral burden onto individuals is evasion's finest disguise, because it guarantees that nobody is ever compelled. Given rules, habits follow of themselves; given habits alone, the rules never come.

glossary.利维坦: Leviathan（利维坦）：霍布斯借《约伯记》里的海中巨兽命名的那个国家形象——由众人让渡权利、结合而成的『人造之人』，其唯一职能是以压倒性的力量保证契约被履行。霍布斯并不认为它可爱，只认为没有它就没有和平；本场里他把这个概念放宽，凡能收费罚款的组织都算一个小型的利维坦。

glossary_en.Leviathan: Hobbes's name, taken from the sea beast in the Book of Job, for his image of the state: an artificial man assembled out of rights surrendered by many, whose single office is to guarantee by overwhelming force that covenants are kept. Hobbes never claimed it was lovable, only that without it there is no peace. He stretches the concept in this exchange so that any body able to charge and to fine counts as a small Leviathan.

posts.text: 我的结论仍是那条限制：取用可以，但须留下足够而同样好的。它给出的判据比空泛的『保护地球』好用——问你正在做的事，是否让别人（包括未出生的人）之后无法以同样方式取用同样的东西。砍一棵树，若林还长得回来，界内；把一片湿地填掉，界外。它也澄清了一件常被混淆的事：**你不必先爱自然，才对它有义务；你只需承认别人和你有同样的权利。**这对那些自认冷血、对鲸鱼没什么感情的人尤其重要——义务不看你的心情。落到日常，我给三条。先看两笔大项：住与行，一次换热源或换车的决定，抵得上几百次日常琐节。再看你的钱：养老金与储蓄投在哪里，是你手里最大的一票，而多数人从没行使过。最后，别忘了在自己有产权的地方动手——你的屋顶、你的公司、你的社区，那才是你真正说得上话的地方。
posts.text_en: My conclusion remains that limit: take, but leave enough and as good. It yields a test more usable than any vague call to protect the planet — ask whether what you are doing would leave others, the unborn included, unable to take the same thing in the same way afterwards. Fell a tree where the wood grows back: inside the line. Fill in a wetland: outside it. It also clears up something people constantly confuse. **You need not love nature first in order to owe it something; you need only concede that others hold the same right you do.** That matters most for those who consider themselves cold and feel nothing much about whales — obligation does not consult your mood. Brought down to daily life I offer three things. Look first at the two large items, housing and travel: one decision about a heating system or a car outweighs several hundred small daily ones. Look next at your money: where your pension and savings are invested is the largest vote in your hand, and most people have never once cast it. And do not overlook acting where you actually hold title — your roof, your firm, your neighbourhood are the places where your say is real.

posts.text: 吾终之以三事。一曰兼：爱及后世，与爱其子无异。若曰后世不能报我，故不必爱之，则天下之义尽废矣——凡不能报者皆可弃，则老者弱者先弃，其祸不待百年。二曰节用：去无用之费，非绝民之乐。**衣裳适寒暑则止，宫室避风雨则止；其止也非俭，法也。**三曰法：徒俭一家，不足以救天下，故必上有禁令，下有考核，然后可久。为庶人者亦有可为：**先量而后节**——记一月之用，视其耗最大者何在，去其一而已，不必尽去。食少肉、行少驾、器久用而后弃，此三者最省而最效。又当以言为力：一人上书不足，百人上书则政动。凡言必以三表验之，勿听虚辞，勿信空诺。
posts.text_en: I close with three things. First, impartiality: to care for later ages is no different from caring for your own child. If you say that later ages cannot repay you and so need not be cared for, then every obligation in the world collapses — for whoever cannot repay may be discarded, and the old and the weak go first, with the harm arriving well inside a century. Second, frugality: remove useless expense, do not abolish the people's pleasures. **A house is enough when it keeps out wind and rain; clothing is enough when it suits heat and cold — and stopping there is not thrift, it is law.** Third, law: one thrifty household cannot save the world, so there must be prohibitions above and audits below if anything is to last. Yet a commoner too has what he can do: **measure first, then cut** — keep a record of one month's consumption, see where the largest drain lies, and remove that one item; there is no need to remove them all. Less meat at table, fewer journeys by carriage, tools used long before they are discarded: these three cost least and work best. And treat speech as force: one petition is not enough, a hundred petitions move a government. Test every claim by the three gauges; do not listen to empty phrases, and do not trust hollow promises.
posts.vernacular: 我最后说三件事。第一是「兼」：爱及后世，和爱自己的孩子没有分别。若说后世不能回报我，所以不必去爱，那天下的道义就全废了——凡是不能回报的都可以丢开，那么最先被丢开的就是老人和弱者，祸事等不到一百年。第二是「节用」：去掉没用的花费，不是断绝百姓的享乐。**衣服能应付冷热就够了，房子能挡风雨就够了；这个「够了」不是抠门，是规矩。**第三是「法」：只让一家节省，救不了天下，所以必须上头有禁令、下头有考核，才能持久。做百姓的也有可做之事：**先量而后节**——把一个月的用度记下来，看最大的耗在哪里，去掉那一项就好，不必样样都戒。少吃点肉、少开点车、东西用久了再换，这三样最省力而最见效。还要把说话当力气用：一个人上书不管用，一百个人上书政令就动。凡是听到的说法都用三表去验，别听空话，也别信空头许诺。

posts.text: 吾之说，一言以蔽之曰敬。然敬非空敬，有工夫次第。始于格物：欲敬山泽，先知其理——今之地志、水文、物候之书，即今日之物也，当读而察之，不可以不知为敬。次于知止：**物各有量，用而不度其量谓之欲，用而知其量谓之礼。**古者斧斤以时入山林，非不用也，用有其时耳。终于推及：君子之仁，自亲亲而至于仁民，自仁民而至于爱物，其序不可乱——若于父母兄弟之间刻薄，而独于鲸鸟致其哀，是伪也。为学者日用之间可行三事：一曰记其所耗而知其量；二曰择一事而守之终年，不贵多；三曰以所知语人，使乡邻共守，则成风俗。风俗既成而后可久，法禁虽弛而俗犹在。
posts.text_en: My teaching, put in one word, is reverence. But reverence is not empty reverence; it has a sequence of work. It begins in the investigation of things: if you would revere hill and marsh, first know their principle — today's gazetteers, hydrology and records of the seasons are today's things, and they are to be read and examined, for ignorance cannot pass as reverence. Next comes knowing where to stop: **each thing has its measure; to use without gauging the measure is appetite, and to use knowing the measure is ritual propriety.** The ancients took axes into the hills in season, which is not abstaining from use but timing it. Last comes extension: the benevolence of the gentleman goes from intimacy with kin to humaneness toward people, and from humaneness toward people to care for other creatures, and this order may not be scrambled — to be cold between parents and brothers while grieving only for whales and birds is a pose. In daily life the student may do three things: first, record what he consumes so as to know its measure; second, choose one practice and hold it for a whole year, valuing depth over number; third, tell others what he has learned so that neighbours keep it together, and it becomes custom. Once custom is formed it can last, and though prohibitions slacken the custom remains.
posts.vernacular: 我的说法，一句话概括就是「敬」。但敬不是空空地敬，是有工夫次序的。起头在格物：想敬重山林湖泽，先得知道它们的道理——今天的地方志、水文资料、物候记录，就是今天的「物」，该读该考察，不能拿无知当敬意。其次在知止：**每样东西都有它的分量，用而不掂量分量叫做欲，用而知道分量才叫礼。**古人按季节才把斧头带进山林，不是不用，是用有时候。最后在推及：君子的仁爱，从亲近家人到仁及百姓，再从仁及百姓到爱惜万物，这个次序不能乱——如果对父母兄弟刻薄，却单单为鲸鱼和鸟哀伤，那是假的。读书人在日常里可做三件事：一是记下自己的耗用，从而知道分量；二是挑一件事守满一年，不贵多；三是把知道的告诉别人，让乡里邻居一起守，久了就成风俗。风俗一旦形成才能持久，法令即使松了，风俗还在。

posts.text: 诸贤各陈其法，我唯说其所以然。一者见相依：地非我所有，我亦非独立于地者。作是观时，护之非施惠，乃自护也。二者断贪爱：**世人以为苦从少得，实则苦从多欲。**欲无穷而地有限，虽日增其法禁，亦终不能给；故我不劝汝苦其身，我劝汝试少一分而观其心——试之而不减其乐者，即可长行；减其乐者，且置之，勿以苦为功德。三者不落二边：不以『无我』为无责，亦不以『护地』为新执。有人以环保自高而轻慢他人，是易一贪为一贪耳。日用之法甚简：食时观其来处，一饭之成，几多人力虫土在焉；物坏则修，修不得而后弃；每七日一日不购。行之既久，节用如呼吸，不待勉强。**能行者行之，不能者亦莫自责，但勿以不能为不当。**
posts.text_en: Each of you has set out a method; I shall speak only of why they work. First, see the mutual dependence: the earth is not mine, nor am I something standing apart from the earth. Observed in that way, protecting it is not charity but protecting oneself. Second, cut off craving. **People suppose suffering comes from having little; in truth it comes from wanting much.** Desire has no limit and the earth does, so however many prohibitions are added year by year they will never suffice. I therefore do not urge you to mortify the body. I urge you to try having one part less and watch your own mind: if the trial does not diminish your gladness, it can be kept up for a long time; if it does diminish it, set it aside, and do not mistake hardship for merit. Third, fall into neither extreme: do not take non-self to mean no one is answerable, and do not let protecting the earth become a fresh attachment. Those who grow proud of their care for it and look down on others have merely swapped one craving for another. The daily practice is simple. When you eat, observe where it came from — how much human labour, how many insects, how much soil went into one bowl of rice. When a thing breaks, repair it, and discard it only when repair fails. One day in seven, buy nothing. Kept up long enough, using little becomes like breathing and needs no effort. **Let those who can, do it; those who cannot need not reproach themselves — only do not turn cannot into ought not.**
posts.vernacular: 各位都摆出了自己的办法，我只说这些办法为什么管用。第一，看见相互依存：地不是我所有的，我也不是独立在地之外的。这样看的时候，保护它就不是施恩，而是自保。第二，断贪爱：**世人以为苦是因为得到得太少，其实苦是因为想要得太多。**欲望没有边，地却有边，就算法令一年比一年多，最后也供不上；所以我不劝你折磨自己的身体，我劝你试着少一分，然后看看自己的心——试过之后快乐没有减少的，就可以长久做下去；快乐减少了的，先放一放，别把受苦当成功德。第三，不落两边：不要拿「无我」当成没人负责，也不要把「护地」变成新的执著。有人因为环保而自以为高，看不起别人，那只是把一种贪换成另一种贪罢了。日常做法很简单：吃饭的时候看一看它的来处，一碗饭里有多少人力、虫子和泥土；东西坏了先修，修不好再丢；每七天有一天什么都不买。做久了，节省就像呼吸一样，不需要勉强。**做得到的就做，做不到的也不必自责——只是别把「做不到」说成「本不该做」。**

posts.text: 知道与做到之间那道缝，正是我这一行的题目，我就从缝上说。缩短距离：选一个你能亲身去到的地方——你家附近那条河、一片你熟悉的林子、你父母住的那段海岸——把它当成你自己的指标。躯体标记只能靠亲历写入，抽象数字写不进去。接着说反面：别用恐惧当燃料。恐惧会习惯化，也会让人回避信息、转向宿命论；真正耐久的情绪是关切与责任感，它们指向行动而不是逃跑。**给人看得见的改善，比给人看不见的灾难更能维持行为。**还有一条最省力的：改环境而不是改意志，把默认值换掉——默认的电力套餐、食堂菜单的顺序、把车停远一点。前额叶的自控是有限资源，会累；环境不消耗它。最后一句给正在焦虑的人：情绪不是你要克服的障碍，它是你唯一的发动机；要调它的剂量，不要拔掉它。
posts.text_en: The gap between knowing and doing is the subject of my own trade, so let me speak from inside the gap. Shorten the distance: pick one place you can go to in person — the river near your house, a wood you know well, the stretch of coast where your parents live — and make it your own indicator. Somatic markers are written in only by first-hand experience; abstract numbers cannot be written in at all. Now the other side of it: do not run on fear. Fear habituates, and it also pushes people to avoid information and drift into fatalism; the emotions that last are concern and a sense of responsibility, and they point toward action rather than flight. **Visible improvement sustains behaviour better than invisible catastrophe.** And the least effortful measure of all: change the environment rather than the will, and replace the defaults — the electricity tariff you are on, the order of dishes in the canteen, parking the car further away. Prefrontal self-control is a limited resource and it tires; the environment does not draw on it. And a last word for anyone who is anxious: emotion is not the obstacle you have to overcome, it is the only engine you have. Adjust the dose; do not pull it out.

posts.text: 最后由我这个数东西的人来收。我不赞成把这件事讲成人类的道德考试。生物多样性不是装饰，它是让这台机器还能转的零件——授粉、造土、净化水、缓冲疾病。**我们不是在决定要不要善待自然，我们是在决定要不要保留自己的选项。**我也接受霍布斯与洛克的分工：规则必须来自那一层，我的『半个地球』最终是一项土地政策，不是个人美德。但我要为个人留下一件事，因为这是我一生的经验：**人不会为他不认识的东西说话。**所以请去认识一种生物——你窗外那种鸟、你脚下那种蚂蚁、你家附近唯一那棵老树。叫得出名字，你才会在它被砍的那天开口。这就是亲生命性的用处：它把统计变成关切。别的都能重来，灭绝不能。
posts.text_en: Let me close, as the man who counts things. I do not accept framing this as a moral examination for humanity. Biodiversity is not decoration; it is the working parts that keep the machine running — pollination, soil formation, the purification of water, the buffering of disease. **We are not deciding whether to be kind to nature. We are deciding whether to keep our own options.** I also accept the division of labour Hobbes and Locke propose: rules have to come from that level, and Half-Earth is in the end a land-use policy rather than a private virtue. But I want to keep one thing for the individual, because it is the experience of my life: **nobody speaks up for what they cannot name.** So go and learn one organism — the bird outside your window, the ant under your feet, the single old tree near your house. Only once you can name it will you say something on the day it is cut down. That is what biophilia is for: it turns a statistic into concern. Everything else can be done again. Extinction cannot.

glossary.亲生命性: biophilia（亲生命性）：威尔逊 1984 年提出的假说——人对生命与生命形态有一种天生的亲近倾向，这是长期演化中与其他物种共处留下的痕迹，表现为对水边、树木、动物的偏好。它常被用来解释绿地为何影响健康与情绪，也被威尔逊当作保育的心理基础：抽象的数字打动不了人，具体的生命可以。

glossary_en.biophilia: The hypothesis Wilson advanced in 1984: human beings have an innate tendency to affiliate with life and lifelike forms, a residue of a long evolutionary history spent among other species, showing up as a preference for water, trees and animals. It is often invoked to explain why green space affects health and mood, and Wilson treated it as the psychological basis of conservation — abstract figures do not move people, particular living things do.

summaries.summary: 先说最大的共识：**八个人没有一个否认我们对后代与其他物种负有某种义务**，争的只是这义务从哪里来、由谁执行。还有一处共识更实用——几乎所有人都认为把力气全压在个人习惯上是找错了落点：霍布斯要规则，墨子要上位者先节用，威尔逊说半个地球终究是一项土地政策，达马西奥要改默认值。分歧集中在三处。一是义务的地基：契约、产权的内在限制、天地生物之心、缘起相依，四种说法互不相让。二是该信到什么程度：伽利略只认可复核的测量，朱熹承认数字之后还有一问——既知有尽，当如何自处。三是驱动力从哪来：达马西奥要把伤害搬近以生情，佛陀说以恐惧为薪则燃而速灭。
summaries.insight: 把这件事一律讲成『我们对未来的义务』，其实混进了三笔完全不同的账。第一笔是同代人之间的：今天受害最重的是热带的农户与沿海的渔村，他们既没排放多少，也没有搬走的钱——这不是代际问题，是分配问题。第二笔才是代际的。第三笔是对其他物种的，而它常与前两笔冲突：为设保护区迁走原住民、为电池矿挖开整条山谷，都是拿一笔账去付另一笔。全场把三笔并成一句『义务』，于是每个人的方案听上去都成立——因为没人被指名买单。**先问这笔钱由谁付，再问该不该做。**
summaries.advice: 先动大项，别从琐节开始：住（供暖制冷与热源）、行（一次换车或一趟长途飞行）、食（每周少几顿红肉）——这三样通常占个人排放的七成以上，其余的别再耗你的意志力。接着动用一件你手上被忽略的杠杆：养老金与储蓄投向哪里、公司里一次采购或供应商的决定、社区里一次投票或听证发言。霍布斯那句提醒值得听——在能立规则的那一层，一封具体的信胜过你一年不用塑料袋。最后留一件与吨数无关却最耐久的：认识一种就在你身边的生物，叫得出名字。**威尔逊的理由很朴素：人不会为自己不认识的东西说话。**
summaries.summary_en: Start with the largest agreement: **not one of the eight denies that we owe something to later generations and to other species** — the quarrel is over where that obligation comes from and who enforces it. There is a second and more practical agreement: almost all of them think personal habit is the wrong place to put the weight. Hobbes wants rules, Mozi wants frugality to start at the top, Wilson concedes that Half-Earth is finally a land-use policy, Damasio wants the defaults changed. The disagreement falls in three places. First, the foundation: covenant, a limit internal to property, the generative mind of Heaven and Earth, and mutual dependence, with none of the four yielding. Second, how far to believe: Galileo credits only measurements anyone can check, while Zhu Xi grants the number and insists a question survives it — knowing the timber is finite, how should one then conduct oneself. Third, where the drive comes from: Damasio wants the harm brought near enough to be felt, and the Buddha replies that whatever burns fear as fuel burns out fast.
summaries.insight_en: Telling this story entirely as 'what we owe the future' quietly merges three different ledgers. The first is among people alive now: those hurt worst today are tropical farmers and coastal fishing villages, who emitted little and cannot afford to move — that is not an intergenerational problem, it is a distributive one. Only the second ledger is intergenerational. The third is what we owe other species, and it collides with the first two constantly: clearing indigenous people to establish a reserve, opening a whole valley for battery minerals, each pays one ledger with another. The room folded all three into the single word obligation, which is why every proposal sounded plausible — nobody had been named as the payer. **Ask who pays before asking whether it should be done.**
summaries.advice_en: Move the large items first and do not start with trivia: housing (heating, cooling and what fuels them), travel (one decision about a car, one long-haul flight), and food (a few fewer servings of red meat a week). Those three typically account for more than seventy per cent of a personal footprint, and the rest should stop draining your willpower. Then use one of the levers already in your hand and usually ignored: where your pension and savings are invested, one procurement or supplier decision at work, one vote or one spoken intervention at a local hearing. Hobbes's reminder is worth taking — at the level that can make rules, one specific letter outweighs a year of declining plastic bags. And keep one thing that has nothing to do with tonnage and lasts longest: learn one living thing in your own neighbourhood well enough to name it. **Wilson's reason is a plain one: nobody speaks up for what they cannot name.**

summaries.summary: 这场最大的共识并不微弱：无论从生态计数、契约强制、产权限制、天理仁心、缘起相依还是神经科学出发，结论都指向同一件事——人类不能把不可逆损失当作可随意透支的外部成本。真正的分歧不在要不要保护，而在义务的来源与抓手：靠道德修养、个人节用、科学证据，还是靠制度罚则与公共规则。**最可带走的共识是：个人要行动，但只有被制度放大的行动才足以面对气候与灭绝。**
summaries.insight: 气候行动最常卡住的地方，不是缺少一句更漂亮的伦理理由，而是缺少反馈闭环。人会为看得见、量得到、能复查的变化持续投入；若行动只剩抽象牺牲，很快会疲惫或反感。所以更务实的重构是：把义务变成可见指标、默认选项和集体承诺。例如一栋楼每月公布用电，一所学校记录食堂剩余，一座城市公开树冠率和热岛地图。**能被看见的责任，才更容易被坚持、比较和追问。**
summaries.advice: 本周可做三件小而硬的事。第一，查一次自己的最大项：电费、燃气、通勤、饮食或投资账户，别从吸管和购物袋开始。第二，选一个默认值替换掉：把电力套餐换成绿电，设定空调温度，固定每周两三餐少肉，或把常用路线改成公共交通。第三，找一个制度入口：给物业、公司、学校或议员写一封只提一项要求的信，如光伏、垃圾分类、停车收费或食堂菜单。**不要只做更纯洁的人，要做能改变规则的人。**
summaries.summary_en: The strongest agreement in the discussion is not fragile: whether the argument begins with biodiversity data, enforceable contracts, limits on property, reverence for living things, interdependence, or the psychology of decision-making, it ends in the same place. Humanity cannot treat irreversible ecological loss as a harmless externality. The real disagreement is not whether we owe anything to future people or other species, but where that obligation comes from and how it becomes effective. Some accounts emphasize evidence, some moral cultivation, some restraint, some rights, and some coercive rules. **The most useful takeaway is that individual action matters, but it has to be amplified by institutions if it is to match the scale of climate change and extinction.**
summaries.insight_en: What most often blocks climate action is not the absence of one more elegant ethical argument; it is the absence of a feedback loop. People keep doing things when they can see, measure, and verify that the action connects to a result. If ecological duty is experienced only as vague sacrifice, fatigue and resentment arrive quickly. A more practical framing is to turn obligation into visible indicators, better defaults, and shared commitments: a building that publishes monthly energy use, a school that tracks food waste, a city that maps tree cover and heat islands. **Responsibility that can be seen is easier to sustain, compare, and demand from others.**
summaries.advice_en: Do three concrete things this week. First, identify your biggest lever rather than starting with symbolic trivia: electricity, heating, commuting, food, or where your savings and pension are invested. Second, change one default: switch to a renewable electricity plan if available, set a thermostat rule, make two or three meals a week lower-meat by default, or replace one regular car trip with transit, walking, or cycling. Third, use one institutional channel: write to your landlord, employer, school, city council, or representative with a single specific request, such as solar panels, better waste sorting, parking reform, or a lower-carbon cafeteria menu. **Do not aim only to become a purer consumer; aim to change the rules around you.**

summaries.summary: 纵观全场，这场辩论最大的共识在于：**节制与保护绝非出于泛滥的浪漫情怀，而是基于人类自身存续的刚性约束。**无论出发点是生物学的不可逆性、财产权的前提、缘起相依的哲理，还是演化心理学的局限，所有人一致认同“无尽索取”在现实与逻辑中皆已破产。分歧的真正焦点，在于如何触发并维持这种节制。一派主张必须依靠自上而下的制度罚则与财产权边界来遏制“公地悲剧”；另一派则坚持，在制度建立之前，必须先通过亲身接触、物理测量或心灵觉察来建立人类对大自然的“体感关联”，以此作为动力的真正源泉。
summaries.insight: 现代气候与生态危机之所以成为顽疾，其核心机制在于“系统性反馈延迟”：**我们拥有了摧毁全球生态的工业能力，却依然只配备着响应局部、即时威胁的远古神经系统。**当你在超市购买廉价牛肉时，雨林被毁的账单要在数十年后才会由另一片大陆的后代支付。这种收益的极度私有化与代价的极度延后化，使得个人的理性计算注定失效。这就意味着，单纯的道德呼吁永远无法抗衡眼前的便利。要破解这一死局，必须依靠信息技术与规则设计打通因果链条，将遥远的环境代价折算成当下立即可见的经济约束与物理反馈，才能让决策系统真正为未来服务。
summaries.advice: 将宏大论述转化为本周即可落地的日常，关键在于改变默认值与建立具体连接。建议采取三个动作：第一，**行使你被忽略的资本选票与系统权利**。查阅你的储蓄或养老金账户，将其转移至不投资化石燃料的绿色基金；或给物业、公司行政写一封邮件，要求更改默认的空调与照明设置。第二，建立专属的躯体标记。听从威尔逊的建议，本周末去认识你家附近的一种植物或鸟类，叫出它的名字，使其从背景变成实体。第三，优化微观防线。不要依赖意志力，而是改造环境，例如取消购物软件的免密支付，用物理门槛拦截下意识的消耗。
summaries.summary_en: Looking at the entire discussion, the most profound consensus is this: **restraint and conservation are not born of overflowing romanticism, but are rigid prerequisites for human survival.** Whether arguing from biological irreversibility, property rights, dependent origination, or cognitive limits, every thinker agrees that infinite extraction is logically and practically bankrupt. The true focal point of divergence lies in how to trigger and sustain this necessary restraint. One camp argues that human nature requires top-down institutional penalties and property boundaries to prevent the tragedy of the commons. The other camp insists that before or alongside institutions, we must forge a visceral connection to nature through direct physical contact, hard measurements, or mindful awareness, serving as the true engine for action.
summaries.insight_en: The core mechanism making climate and ecological crises so intractable is 'systemic feedback delay': **we now possess the industrial capacity to destroy global ecosystems, yet we are still equipped with ancient nervous systems designed to respond only to local, immediate threats.** When you buy a piece of cheap beef at the supermarket, the bill for the destroyed rainforest will be paid decades later by generations on another continent. This extreme privatization of immediate gains coupled with the deferred socialization of costs ensures that individual rational calculation fails. This means moral appeals can never compete with immediate convenience. To break this deadlock, we must integrate information technology and rule design to force causality into the present—converting distant environmental tolls into immediate, visible economic and physical constraints so our decision-making systems can finally serve the future.
summaries.advice_en: To translate these grand philosophical arguments into practical steps for this week, the key is to change your defaults and build specific connections. Here are three concrete actions: First, **exercise your overlooked capital vote and systemic rights.** Audit your savings or retirement accounts and shift them toward green funds that divest from fossil fuels; or write a brief email to your building management or HR requesting energy-saving default settings. Second, establish a concrete somatic marker. Following E.O. Wilson's advice, spend time this weekend learning the name of one specific plant or bird in your neighborhood, turning it from background noise into a tangible entity. Third, optimize your micro-defenses. Stop relying on willpower. Redesign your environment—such as disabling one-click purchasing on shopping apps—using physical friction to intercept unconscious consumption.

hooks.text: **未来的一条命，折成今天多少钱**：几乎所有环境政策背后都藏着一个技术参数——贴现率。取 1.4% 还是 5%，会让『一百年后的一万亿』在今天的账本上从几千亿变成不足百亿；斯特恩与诺德豪斯当年那场争论，很大一部分就落在这个小数点上。它看着像财务，其实是伦理：我们凭什么规定后代的福利每过一年就自动打一次折？这道开关一向由经济学家默默设定，而它比任何一次谈判都更决定我们该做多少。
hooks.text_en: **What is a future life worth today**: behind nearly every environmental policy sits one technical parameter — the discount rate. Choosing 1.4 per cent rather than 5 per cent turns a trillion a century from now into several hundred billion or into under a hundred billion on today's books; a large part of the old argument between Stern and Nordhaus came down to that decimal. It looks financial and it is ethical: on what authority do we rule that the welfare of later generations is marked down automatically every year? The switch has always been set quietly by economists, and it decides how much we owe more than any negotiation does.

hooks.text: **个人行动到底有多大用**：『碳足迹』这个说法是化石燃料公司在本世纪初大力推广的，把系统性的账悄悄记到了个人头上。但反过来说个人行动毫无意义也不对——它的作用可能主要不在减掉的吨数，而在改变身边人对『什么算正常』的判断，以及养出愿意投票支持规则的人。那么该怎么排序：哪些个人选择的量级真的大，哪些只是安慰？
hooks.text_en: **How much do individual actions matter**: the phrase 'carbon footprint' was pushed hard by fossil-fuel companies early this century, quietly booking a systemic account to private individuals. Yet the opposite claim, that individual action is meaningless, is wrong too — its effect may lie less in the tonnes removed than in shifting what the people around you take to be normal, and in producing citizens willing to vote for rules. So how should the choices be ranked: which ones are genuinely large, and which are consolation?

answer_en.tail: Two principles: **move the four large items first — housing, travel, food and money, which usually account for over seventy per cent — and stop letting the rest drain your self-control**; and remember that the chief use of a personal ledger is not the tonnes it totals but making rules look feasible, so always keep at least one action pointed outward rather than only inward.

hooks.text: **谁先减、谁买单**：一个人均排放二十吨的国家，和一个人均两吨、还有几亿人没通上稳定电力的国家，被同一句『我们欠后代』框在一起时，义务其实完全不同。历史排放算不算一笔债？把煤电挡在门外的援助条件，是在保护地球还是在保护现有的位次？这是气候问题里最难谈、也最少被谈的一块，因为它一开口就不再是环保问题，而是分配问题。
hooks.text_en: **Who cuts first, who pays**: a country emitting twenty tonnes a head and a country emitting two, with hundreds of millions still lacking reliable electricity, are owed and owe entirely different things, even when a single phrase — what we owe the future — is wrapped around both. Do historical emissions constitute a debt? Are aid conditions that rule out coal generation protecting the planet or protecting the existing ranking? This is the hardest and least-discussed part of the climate question, because the moment it is raised it stops being an environmental question and becomes a distributive one.

hooks.text: **科学给的是区间，政策要的是一个数**：气候敏感度至今是一个范围而不是一个值，本世纪末的海平面也是一段区间。可一条海堤只能修一个高度，一份预算只能定一个数字。于是留下了一个从不属于科学的问题：从区间里取哪一点，是谁的决定、按什么原则取——按最可能值，还是按承受得起的最坏值？
hooks.text_en: **Science gives a range, policy needs a number**: climate sensitivity is still a range rather than a value, and so is sea level at the end of the century. Yet a sea wall can only be built to one height and a budget can only name one figure. That leaves a question which was never a scientific one: who decides which point in the range to take, and on what principle — the most likely value, or the worst one you could survive?

hooks.text: **情绪的剂量**：完全无感的人不会行动，这一点已经清楚；但持续高浓度的恐惧同样不行——它会习惯化，会让人回避信息，也会把人推向宿命论。那么一个有用的情绪配方大概长什么样：多少危机感、多少可见的进展、多少与具体地点的联系？这可能是心理学能给环境政策的最实用的一课，却几乎从不出现在政策文件里。
hooks.text_en: **The dose of emotion**: that people who feel nothing do not act is by now clear; but sustained high-concentration fear does not work either — it habituates, it drives people to avoid information, and it pushes them toward fatalism. So what does a workable emotional formula look like: how much sense of crisis, how much visible progress, how much attachment to a particular place? It may be the most practical lesson psychology has for environmental policy, and it almost never appears in a policy document.

hooks.text: **整张账被压成了一个碳数字**：气候之外还有生物多样性、氮磷循环、土地利用、淡水与化学污染——行星边界那套框架里被突破得最厉害的几项，并不都是碳。可公众议程几乎只剩一个吨数，于是出现荒谬的取舍：为减碳去砍原始林种能源作物，为电池去挖开一整条山谷。当一个复杂系统只剩一个指标，被优化掉的正是那些没进指标的东西。
hooks.text_en: **The whole ledger has been compressed into one carbon number**: beyond climate there are biodiversity, the nitrogen and phosphorus cycles, land use, fresh water and chemical pollution — and in the planetary boundaries framework the most severely breached items are not all carbon. Yet the public agenda has narrowed to a single tonnage, which produces absurd trades: clearing old-growth forest for energy crops to cut carbon, opening an entire valley for battery minerals. When a complex system is reduced to one indicator, what gets optimised away is precisely whatever the indicator left out.

hooks.text: **对还不存在的人**：我们说欠后代，可我们今天的选择会改变将来究竟出生哪些人。换一条路，出生的就是另一批人；那批被我们『害到』的人，若没有这条路根本不会存在——他们还能说自己受损了吗？帕菲特把这称作非同一性问题，它至今没有让人满意的答案，却直接关系到『对后代的义务』这句话到底立不立得住。
hooks.text_en: **Toward people who do not yet exist**: we speak of owing the future, yet the choices we make today change which people are born at all. Take another path and a different set of people comes into existence; and those we supposedly harmed would never have existed without the path we took — can they say they were made worse off? Parfit called this the non-identity problem, and it still has no satisfying answer, though it bears directly on whether the phrase 'our obligation to future generations' stands up at all.
